title: Linking through unique identifier in motion alert
description: The real-time motion alert may contain device identifiers or user identifiers that could be used to link data to specific individuals across systems.

title: Quasi-identifier combining in motion data
description: Motion data combined with other attributes (time, location, device type) could serve as quasi-identifiers to link data to individuals.

title: Processing of identified data in motion alerts
description: The motion alert may contain identified information about the user or device that is being processed and forwarded.

title: Revealing attributes in motion data
description: Motion data may reveal revealing attributes such as location patterns, activity times, or behavioral patterns that support identification of the data subject.

title: Data type sensitivity - motion data may be more sensitive than needed
description: Motion data could be perceived as highly sensitive personal data, and may be collected/processed when strictly not required for the functional purpose.
assumptions: Motion data is considered sensitive personal data

title: Data propagation to mobile app backend
description: Motion data is propagated from Home Hub to Mobile App Backend where it may be accessible by parties beyond what is functionally necessary.
assumptions: Mobile App Backend may have broader access than Home Hub

title: Unawareness of motion data processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their motion data is being collected, processed, and forwarded to the mobile app backend.
assumptions: Users are not informed about motion data collection

title: Lack of control over motion data preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their motion data is processed and shared.
assumptions: No granular consent controls for motion data

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Motion data may be processed beyond what is actually needed for the functional purpose of forwarding alerts.
assumptions: Motion data collection exceeds functional requirements

title: Identifier in notification routing
description: The motion-detected notification contains identifiers (e.g., user ID, phone number) to route to the specific homeowner, enabling identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Notification must include routing information to reach the correct homeowner device.

title: Revealing attributes in motion data
description: Motion detection data reveals when and where the homeowner is present, which are revealing attributes that support identification of the data subject's location and activity patterns.
assumptions: Motion detection inherently captures presence/absence information.

title: System response reveals motion detection
description: The notification itself is a system response that reveals motion was detected, potentially exposing the homeowner's presence or activity at a specific time.
assumptions: Notification delivery confirms motion detection occurred.

title: Potentially sensitive motion data
description: Motion detection data may be perceived as sensitive as it reveals presence/absence patterns, home routines, and occupancy information that could be misused.
assumptions: Motion data can infer sensitive behavioral patterns about the homeowner.

title: Potential unnecessary data treatment
description: Motion detection data may be analyzed, enriched, or processed beyond what is strictly needed for sending a simple notification (e.g., pattern analysis, storage for future use).
assumptions: Backend may process motion data beyond notification delivery.
uncertainty_note: Depends on backend processing logic not fully specified.

title: Unawareness of motion detection processing
description: The homeowner may not be aware that motion detection is actively processing their data and sending notifications, especially if the feature is enabled by default or not clearly disclosed.
assumptions: Users may not understand the extent of motion data collection.

title: Lack of control over notification preferences
description: The homeowner may lack control to customize when, how, or how long motion detection notifications are processed (e.g., no granular preferences for notification frequency or sensitivity).
assumptions: Notification settings may be limited or not user-configurable.

title: Potential violation of data minimization
description: Motion detection data may be processed beyond what is actually needed for the functional goal of sending a simple notification (e.g., storing historical motion data, analyzing patterns).
assumptions: Data minimization principle requires only necessary data processing.
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual backend processing scope.
